So people always ask me: why can't I understand series? I've studied English for years. And the answer is, the writers want their characters to sound like real people, and real people use slang. In Australia we say arvo for afternoon, and no worries for almost everything. In London they say innit. You won't find these in a grammar book. My advice? Don't stop the episode every time you hear a new word. Pick it up from the context, write it down, and check it later. And be patient with accents. In my experience, it takes about three or four episodes to catch on. After that, your ear just adjusts.

Here's the method I give all my students, and it works at any level. Choose one scene, not a whole episode. Two or three minutes. First, watch it with English subtitles, so you know what's happening. Second, watch it again with no subtitles at all. You'll be surprised how much you can make out now. Third, and this is the important part, close your eyes and just listen. If there's a line you can't catch, rewind, but no more than three times. Then move on. That third step trains your ear for the real speed, with no help from your eyes. Ten minutes a day, and in two months you'll hear the difference.
